paragraphs: Hyman describes her as the one woman, out of all the daughters of Israel mentioned in the two Talmuds, who merited to take part in halakhah together with the great Tannaim of the generation.

Hyman says that she was the daughter of the Tanna renowned for his righteousness, R' Chanina ben Teradyon, who was killed for the sanctification of God's Name, one of the martyrs of the government. While still in her youth she showed that she was a great and learned woman, as is brought in Eruvin 53b: Rabbi Yose the Galilean was walking along the road and met Beruriah. He said to her, 'By which way do we go to Lod?' She said to him, 'Foolish Galilean! Did the Sages not say, "Do not talk much with a woman"? You should have said, "Which to Lod?"' And, as Hyman says is well known, Rabbi Yose the Galilean was a colleague of R' Akiva; therefore, he concludes, this must necessarily have been in her youth.

And in the Tosefta of Kelim, Bava Metzia, chapter 1, they said: Regarding a kalustra (a door fitting), R' Tarfon declares it impure while the Sages declare it pure, and Beruriah says: one removes it from this doorway and hangs it on another on Shabbat. When her words were stated before R' Yehoshua — and Hyman reports the Gra’s reading as R' Yehudah [ben Bava] — he said, 'Beruriah has spoken well.'

Hyman quotes: And in the Tosefta of Kelim, Bava Kamma, chapter 4, halakhah 9: An oven — from when is its purification? R' Chalafta of Kfar Chananya said: I asked Shimon ben Chananyah, who had asked R' Chanina ben Teradyon, and he said: from when it is moved from its place; but his daughter says: from when they strip off its sheath. When these statements were made before R' Yehudah ben Bava, he said, 'His daughter has spoken better than he.'

notes.text: The supplied final מהוא is comparative: his daughter’s statement is better than his. The doorway discussion is about a door fitting, not a generic vessel hung on a fellow’s person.

The precise kalustra/Tosefta wording still requires a matching named edition. Gra’s Yehuda versus Yehoshua and Hyman’s bracketed ben Bava remain meaningful variants. The youth and unique-woman claims are Hyman’s.

The fresh William Davidson Eruvin 53b paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Yose the Galilean and preserves the question to Beruriah and her shorter suggested wording; his full Rabbi title has local support. The other source-abbreviated titles in the new English remain R' without transferring fuller titles between people or passages. Hyman’s claim that she was the one woman to participate with the great Tannaim, and his emphatic inference that this necessarily happened in her youth, remain his statements at full strength. The older parenthetical Roman gloss is not repeated in the new body; the supplied Hebrew speaks of the government. The attempted named Tosefta chapter and oven-paragraph requests returned no text. They provide no evidence for the precise kalustra wording, Gra’s reported Yehudah/Yehoshua variant or Hyman’s bracketed [ben Bava]; these remain unresolved and p003 remains held. The door-fitting wording, doorway-to-doorway direction, question-and-report chain, and comparative ‘His daughter has spoken better than he’ are retained as Hyman’s supplied text and earlier local reading. Both existing mixed notes remain verbatim; no new edition collation, printed correction history, genealogy, chronology or identity admission is claimed. No additional legal material or people from the fresh Eruvin paragraph are imported.

The supplied part of Hyman’s Beruriah article matches the printed passage in volume I, page 294; the printed biography continues beyond this supplied text. Subsequent consultation of the correctly named Tosefta Kelim Metzia, chapter 1, recovered the complete door-fitting paragraph: the Machon Mamre Hebrew and Community English put the praise before Rabbi Yehoshua. This supports the doorway-to-doorway wording, while Hyman’s reported Gra reading Yehudah and bracketed [ben Bava] remain attributed; that exact apparatus has not been collated. The consulted Kelim Kamma 4:9 Hebrew says that Shimon asked the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon, whereas Hyman’s quotation says that he asked Rabbi Chanina himself. Its English concludes that the daughter spoke better than his son and reports a Vienna/Gra reading in a footnote; Hyman’s supplied comparison is “better than he.” His quotation is preserved with explicit attribution rather than silently replaced. The editorial manuscript report is not an independent inspection of those witnesses. Hyman’s unique-woman claim and necessary-youth inference remain his claims, without a new chronology or family identification.
